## Natural history notes

A small sharpshooter leafhopper characterized by its slender green body, wedge-shaped profile, clear wings, and pale spots or markings that help distinguish it from other green sharpshooters. In Florida, it is found on grasses, sedges, rushes, and other low vegetation in wetlands, marsh edges, wet prairies, ditches, fields, and other moist open habitats. It feeds by piercing plant tissue and drinking xylem sap, while also serving as prey for spiders, assassin bugs, birds, and other insect-eating animals.
